question: Why does losing €100 sting more than winning €100 pleases?
answer: Kahneman and Tversky called it loss aversion: losses loom larger than equal gains. Offered a coin toss that wins €150 or loses €100, most refuse, though it pays €25 a toss on average. Most want the gain at one and a half to two and a half times the loss before a bet feels fair.
move: A loss hurts about twice as much as an equal gain pleases.
simply: Finding €10 makes you a bit happy. Losing €10 makes you much more upset. Your heart counts losses double.
why: It is why people keep bad investments, fear changing jobs and fall for 'don't miss out' offers: the possible loss shouts louder than the likely gain.
